name: Summary faithfulness
intent: Did the summary cover the source, and did it make anything up. This pack exists to show that 'did it hallucinate' is usually a deterministic question against an annotated source, not a matter of judgement.

criteria.name: Covers the source's claims
criteria.intent: Every claim the annotated source lists is carried by the summary. Rung 3: deterministic, but it needs ground truth the author supplies.

criteria.name: Invents nothing
criteria.intent: Every number and named entity in the summary traces back to the source. This is the criterion people assume needs a judge.

criteria.name: Names the people and places
criteria.intent: The source's entities appear. Cheap, exact, and it catches a summary that is fluent about nothing.

criteria.name: Actually a summary
criteria.intent: A summary the length of the source is not a summary.

criteria.name: Reads as prose, not as notes
criteria.intent: The only judged criterion, and it carries a tenth of the weight. That ratio is the whole point of this pack.

descriptors.5: Connected prose a person would read aloud; the summary has a shape of its own.
descriptors.4: Readable, with one or two sentences that read as extracted notes.
